diseases.name: Cercospora Leaf Spot
diseases.description: A fungal leaf spot of eggplant with angular, yellow-edged spots.
diseases.causes: Spores survive on debris and spread by wind and rain in warm, humid weather.
symptoms: Small, angular to round yellow spots
Spots turn brown with a grey centre
diseases.effect: Leaf loss lowers yield and exposes fruit to sun.

steps.title: Remove spotted leaves
steps.instruction: Pick off spotted leaves when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: eggplant cercospora leaf spot

diseases.name: Phomopsis Blight and Fruit Rot
diseases.description: A fungal disease of eggplant that rots the fruit and spots the leaves and stems.
diseases.causes: Spores come in on seed and debris and spread by rain splash in hot, wet weather.
symptoms: Pale, sunken, soft spots on the fruit
Spots enlarge with rings of tiny black dots (spore bodies)
Round grey-brown leaf spots; stem cankers
diseases.effect: Rotting fruit is lost, in the field and after harvest.
diseases.untreated: Can destroy a large part of the crop.

steps.title: Remove rotting fruit
steps.instruction: Pick off rotting fruit when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

lifecycle: The fungus comes in on seed and debris.
Rain splashes spores onto fruit and leaves.
Pale sunken spots form on the fruit.
Rings of black spore bodies spread it on.

diseases.name: Phytophthora Blight
diseases.description: A water-mould disease that rots eggplant fruit and can collapse whole plants.
diseases.causes: The water mould lives in the soil and spreads in water: rain splash, standing water and irrigation; worst on poorly drained soil.
symptoms: Water-soaked, dark patches on the fruit
White, cottony growth on the rotting fruit
Dark stem lesions at the soil; plants wilt and die
diseases.effect: Fruit rots and plants can be killed.
diseases.untreated: Infested fields stay infested for years.

steps.title: Remove rotting fruit and dead plants
steps.instruction: Pick off rotting fruit and dead plants when the plants are dry and take them away.

steps.title: Improve drainage
steps.instruction: Raise beds and avoid standing water.
steps.rationale: The water mould spreads in water.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered product for Phytophthora on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

prevention.title: Rotate away from peppers, cucurbits and tomato

lifecycle: The water mould survives in soil.
Splash and standing water carry spores to plants.
Fruit rots with white mould; stems get lesions.
Plants wilt and spores spread in water.
